tieuDeEn: Orchids and chrysanthemums are the pride of the world: good flowers make the plant more precious, and many flowers make the scent stronger. Brothers and sisters are like one pot of flowers – live in harmony to make your parents happy.

dichXuoi.en: Chrysanthemums and orchids are beautiful, treasured flowers. Good flowers make the plant more precious; many flowers make the scent even sweeter.

dichXuoi.en: Brothers and sisters in one home are as close as one pot of flowers. Live kindly and lovingly together to make your parents happy.

en: Cô Hà welcomes you to lesson twenty-four of “Lên Tám”. Last time we admired the lively image of orchids and chrysanthemums growing in one pot. Today we'll see what the beauty and fragrance of those flowers bring to life, and the deep lesson the poet wants to give about how siblings should treat each other. Listen to today's two verses.
Chrysanthemums and orchids are the glory of this world; good flowers make the plant more precious, and many flowers make the scent stronger.
Brothers and sisters in one home are as close as a pot of flowers; live in such harmony that you make your parents happy.

The poem praises nature's beauty: orchids and chrysanthemums are noble flowers that bring colour and scent to life. Then it gives a lovely rule: when the flowers bloom healthy and bright, people value the plant that grew them even more; when many flowers bloom at once, their scents mix and spread further. In the same way, good and capable children bring honour to their whole family and clan.

So the next verse sums up a precious lesson. “Hữu ái” means the close, peaceful love between siblings or good friends, always caring for and giving way to each other. The poem teaches that parents' greatest reward and happiness isn't money – it's seeing their children live in harmony under one roof, helping each other study and never fighting or quarrelling. Living in harmony is the best way to repay your parents.
